options.title: Precompute word 0 in the frame source
options.approach: In frame_src, hold the s_valid/s_data word 0 ready from the configuration so s_valid rises together with `start` instead of one clock later (stage fs_start). Word 0 depends only on the configuration, and the preamble does not depend on frame data. The IP and UDP checksum logic, the MAC and the PCS are not changed.

gain.basis_note: fs_start adds 1 clock and the stage file allows 1 to be removed, so at most 1 clock is saved. The low end is 0 because the MAC may need s_valid one clock later.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Small RTL change. The worst setup path (0.115 ns) ends in frame_src (ip_csum), so placement may shift and the build may need a repeat.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Merge receive extraction and descramble
options.approach: In pcs_rx, put the gearbox and block extraction (rx_blk) and the descramble and decode (rx_descramble) in front of one register. This removes the stage B register. The block-lock FSM and the MAC are not changed.

gain.basis_note: rx_descramble adds 1 clock and the stage file allows at most 1 to be removed. The low end is 0 because the merged path may fail timing and the merge would have to be undone.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Timing is the main risk. The stage description says the 192-bit shifter plus the 64-bit XOR tree did not close at 161 MHz in design. Expect several rounds.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Shorten the go-pulse crossing by one flop
options.approach: In core, shorten the receive-to-transmit go-pulse crossing (cross_go, xpm_cdc_pulse u_p_go) by one clock, for example by dropping the output register after the edge detect. Check that the order bus beside the pulse is still settled when frame_src samples it. The synchroniser flops that guard metastability are not touched.

gain.basis_note: cross_go adds 4 clocks and the stage file allows 1 to be removed, so the saving is at most 1 clock. The low end is 0 because an earlier pulse may find the order bus unsettled.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The RTL change is small. Showing the crossing is safe needs a CDC report and a board run.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Slack-driven stage merging across the whole chain
options.approach: Remove or merge the register stages that have the most post-route slack: rx_descramble, decide, fs_start and mac_preamble. Then check timing and keep only the merges that close. The crossing stage, the gearbox spill and the encode register stay as they are. The GT and optics share of the board latency is frozen and not addressed.

gain.basis_note: The four stages each allow 1 removable clock, so at most 4 of the 11 total clocks. The slacks are 2.215, 1.735, 1.428 and 1.132 ns, and a merge that uses that slack may still fail timing. The low end of 1 assumes only one merge closes.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (4)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Each merge is a separate timing experiment, and merging in the same clock domain can move the worst path.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run
